newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pro and anti-Le Pen demonstrations in France.
newsitem.headline: Pro and anti-Le Pen demonstrations in France.

text.p: Demonstrators for or against extreme rightist leader Jean-Marie Le Pen took to the streets in the French port of Dunkirk and the city of Toulouse on Saturday but no clashes were reported.

Some 700 sympathisers of Le Pen's National Front Party arrived by train in Dunkirk to protest against suspended jail terms levelled against two NF regional councillors for incitement to racial discrimination in a local party publication.
An equal number of inhabitants of the Channel port demonstrated simultaneously against the rightists' rally while police patrolled to prevent the two groups from meeting.
Up to 1,300 people rallied in the streets of the southwest French city of Toulouse to protest against the holding of an NF rally there later in the day which Le Pen was due to address.
The anti-immigrant leader is credited with about 15 percent of voting intentions among the French public and recently created new controversy by saying not all races were equal.

Earlier in the day, veterans of the Spanish Civil War, marking near Paris the 60th anniversary of the creation of the International Brigades, warned of future civil strife in France if Le Pen was not stopped.
